attributes.command: git show --stat HEAD | tail -18; git status --short; git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -3

body.text:
Everything's committed and pushed (`79b6209..8a2fdff`). Three things landed, and the investigation turned up something you'll want to decide on.

## 1. The hang — it wasn't hanging, it was taking 123 seconds

Not one slow git command: **thousands of git processes**. Every commit's identity lookup re-read the entire change-map with one `cat-file` per change; notes and sessions were read one spawn at a time too. At ~25–30ms per spawn on Windows, that's the whole two minutes.

Fixed by batching (`catFileBatch` over `git cat-file --batch`, plus snapshot/bulk readers for the change-map, notes and sessions). Same walk now takes **1.2s**, and `/api/overview` answers in 0.66s. `/api/overview` also now defaults to the most recent 300 commits — a page must open promptly on a 50,000-commit repo; `git for-ai report` still walks everything.

The subtle part worth knowing about: git's batch protocol frames objects by *byte* length, and this repo's ledger is full of em-dashes — a character-indexed parser would corrupt every object after the first multi-byte one. There's a test for exactly that.

## 2. The UI stopped narrating itself

Gone from the screen: the footer about a read-only server on 127.0.0.1 and what agents use instead, "never inferred or fabricated", and the internal vocabulary (ledger, change-map, spans, "captured intent"). In its place: "no reasoning recorded", "session recording on", "Merge commit — showing what it brought in". The honesty is unchanged — every missing-data state is still labeled and still true; only the essay defending it is gone. Recorded as CLAUDE.md rule 10 so it doesn't creep back.

Also caught in passing: the ask panel told users to run `git for-ai index`, which isn't a command.

## 3. Desktop step 4b — the actions panel

Six endpoints (doctor, reindex, sync, annotate, relink, reconcile), each a thin wrapper over the same pure function its CLI command uses. They don't exist without a launch token, so `git for-ai review` stays exactly as read-only as before. Token is minted per launch, handed to the Electron renderer in the URL fragment, never served by any endpoint, checked in constant time, required in a header. Actions run as jobs with progress, one at a time, and pushing needs an explicit confirmation.

**Left out deliberately:** annotate, relink and reconcile are served but have no UI — annotate needs a real form, and the repair verbs belong on attention items. That's the next increment, and it's written down as such.

655 tests green; verified live (401 without token, 202 with, doctor completing, push refused unconfirmed, `/api/meta` not leaking the token).

## The `ask` failure — root cause found, and it needs your call

The model wasn't being unhelpful. It was given eleven words and honestly refused.

`LedgerEntry.scope` — the per-file list of what a change touched — **is** captured on every commit, and the right ledger entry for HEAD *was* retrieved (rank 9, via the recency floor). But `renderSource()` never puts `scope` into the synthesis prompt, and `ledgerText()` never puts it into the indexed text. All the model received for that source was the commit's summary line. Nothing in the index is keyed by commit at all, so no retrieval tuning fixes this alone.

(Separately: the index is 3 commits stale — but the recency floor covered that, so staleness didn't cause this.)

Two fixes, and I'd do both:

- **Render `scope` into the prompt** — a few lines in `synthesis.ts`. Fixes every ledger-sourced answer, works immediately even on a stale index. Near-zero risk.
- **Recognise commit-scoped questions and answer from git directly** — "what changed in the last commit" is one `git show` away and always exact. Precedent exists: `blame --why` already treats git as ground truth and the index as supplementary. Medium effort; the diff plumbing from today's `/api/diff/:sha` is already there.

Want me to do both, just the cheap one, or push on with the desktop work (annotate form + guided repair, then packaging)?

You're right, and that's a better design than what I proposed. Pre-classifying questions to decide what to stuff into context is guessing at the model's needs; the tool already has `show`, `log --intent`, `blame --why`, and now `diff` as first-class capabilities — and it exposes them to *other* agents over MCP. Its own `ask` should be a client of the same toolbox, deciding what it needs and fetching it.

Let me check the API shape before I write the loop:

The skill confirms the loop shape. One deviation I'll note up front: this repo deliberately uses raw `fetch` with an injectable `fetchImpl` (CLAUDE.md rule 1 — the single sanctioned mock seam), so I'm extending that rather than introducing the SDK.

body.text:
Yes — worth stopping. Honest read on scope:

This isn't a tweak to synthesis, it's a change in kind: single-shot "here are your sources, answer" becomes an agentic loop where the model calls back into git. It needs a new tool-injection seam (core defines the interface, the CLI supplies implementations, because core can't import CLI), changes at three call sites (`ask`, `/api/ask`, the MCP tool), a per-call iteration/cost cap, and tests through the `fetchImpl` seam. That's the same size as the desktop step I just finished.

Two things make now the right moment: nothing is half-built (I haven't edited a file for this yet), and this session is long — the next one starts sharper.

But a pasted prompt is a weak handoff for this repo. The investigation findings only exist in this conversation, and CLAUDE.md says nontrivial surfaces get a spec first. So let me spend the rest of this session writing that spec into the repo, where the next session can find it via the tool's own ledger:

attributes.command:
git add architecture/ASK_TOOLS.md architecture/ROADMAP.md && git commit -F - <<'MSG'
Spec: ask should use the tool's own features, not a context-stuffing guess

A live failure: "tell me what changed in the last commit" came back as an
honest refusal. Investigated before designing anything.

Root cause, with evidence: retrieval WORKED - the recency floor put HEAD's
own ledger entry in front of the model at rank 9. But LedgerEntry.scope,
the per-file list of what a change touched (31 real files on that entry),
never reaches the prompt: renderSource() builds each source from a header
plus chunk.text, and ledgerText() builds the indexed text from summary +
reasoning. Neither reads scope. The literal string the model got for HEAD
was its eleven-word summary line. With a system prompt that says "answer
from the sources ONLY, and say so plainly if they don't answer", the
refusal is the correct behaviour. Nothing in the index is keyed by commit
at all, so this class of question is unreachable by retrieval tuning.
Affects ask, /api/ask and the MCP ask tool alike - one engine.

The obvious fix - classify commit-shaped questions and pre-fetch a diff
into the prompt - is rejected, at the owner's direction: "the ask
functionality should be able to use the git for-ai features itself, that
is partly the point. i dont think we should be preemptively guessing what
the ask needs to shove it into context right?" That's right. A classifier
is us guessing ahead of time, with a keyword list to maintain forever,
covering only the question shapes we thought of - while this project
already exposes show / log_intent / blame_why / diff as MCP tools FOR
OTHER AGENTS. Its own answering path should be a client of that toolbox.

So: synthesis becomes an agentic tool loop. Retrieval still runs and still
supplies numbered citable sources; on top of it the model calls back into
git for what it decides it needs. Core defines the tool interface and owns
the loop, the CLI injects implementations wrapping the same pure run*
functions its commands use (core cannot import CLI - hard rule 6).

The spec records what must not break: the raw-fetch/fetchImpl seam (no
SDK), honest degradation including a labeled outcome when the loop hits
its cap, ask staying a read, multi-call cost with an iteration cap, and
tool-call provenance surfaced rather than hidden - an answer grounded in
`git show` is MORE verifiable than one grounded in an embedding hit.

Also captured as cheap adjacent work: render scope into renderSource. That
is not the rejected guessing - it renders a record we already retrieved
completely instead of truncating it to its summary line, and it works on a
stale index.

No code yet. Speccing first per CLAUDE.md, and stopping here deliberately:
nothing is half-built, and the next session starts against this document
rather than a pasted summary.
